decisive_items: Hypercellular marrow consisting of 80% plasma cells with atypical morphology and κ-light-chain restriction
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
response.rationale: Bone marrow plasma cell infiltration, monoclonal IgG-κ, lytic lesions, hypercalcemia, and renal injury together establish multiple myeloma as the unifying diagnosis; cryoglobulinemia and hypercalcemia are secondary manifestations rather than primary etiologies.

rejected.why: Elevated cryoglobulins explain skin findings but are a consequence of the underlying plasma cell dyscrasia, not the primary diagnosis.
Amyloidosis lacks confirmatory biopsy evidence (no Congo red or apple-green birefringence); biopsy shows cryoglobulin-fibrin thrombi.
Hypercalcemia and lytic lesions are features of multiple myeloma, not an independent diagnosis.
